title: Intro
subtitle: Open the door. Build trust.
goal: Confirm who you are speaking with, set the purpose of the call, and earn permission to ask questions.
script: Before I throw numbers at you, I want to make sure I understand what you are trying to accomplish and what would actually make this worth it for you.
checklist: Provide required licensing or company disclosure
State the purpose of the call
Ask permission to review their refinance goals
prompts: What made you open to looking at a refinance right now?
If this call goes well, what would you want to walk away knowing?

title: Discovery
subtitle: Ask. Listen. Understand.
goal: Collect the facts and the motivation before discussing loan structure.
script: The numbers only matter if they solve the right problem, so I am going to ask a few quick questions first.
checklist: Ask what happens if they do nothing
prompts: Is your main priority lowering payment, shortening term, or accessing cash?
What is your current monthly mortgage payment?
Do you know your current rate and approximate balance?
What would need to improve for this to feel worth moving forward?

title: Recap
subtitle: Clarify. Confirm. Align.
goal: Repeat the borrower goal back before presenting any solution.
script: Just to make sure we are on the same page, your main priority is [goal], and ideally we want to get [payment, cash, term, or certainty outcome]. Did I get that right?
checklist: Get verbal alignment before quoting numbers
prompts: What is the most important part of this for you?
Is there anything I missed before I show you the option?

title: Set the Stage
subtitle: Prepare their mind.
goal: Explain how to evaluate the offer before showing the approval details.
script: When we look at this, I do not want you judging it only by rate. I want us to look at payment impact, total cost, break-even, and whether it solves the reason you took this call.
checklist: Remind them of their stated goal
Mention market movement without making predictions
Prepare them for payment, cost, and break-even discussion
prompts: The question is not just 'is the rate lower?' The question is whether the structure improves your situation enough to justify moving forward.

title: Mic Drop Close
subtitle: Own the value. Make it easy.
goal: Present the approval in a simple, confident way and ask for the decision.
script: Based on what you told me, this option does what we set out to do: it targets [goal], gives you [benefit], and keeps the decision grounded in the numbers we just reviewed. Does this sound like the solution we discussed?
checklist: Ask a direct closing question, then pause
prompts: Cash to close or lender credit:

title: Rebuttal Hub
subtitle: Play defense. Remove doubt.
goal: Address hesitation without sounding defensive or dismissive.
script: Most objections are requests for more certainty. Slow down, validate the concern, and bring the conversation back to the borrower's original goal.

rebuttals.label: Just tell me the rate
rebuttals.response: I will share the exact rate right now—I just need 60 seconds to confirm your balance and goal so I quote you a real, accurate structure instead of a bait-and-switch teaser.
rebuttals.followUp: Are you mainly looking to drop the monthly payment or pull cash out?

rebuttals.label: Rates might drop
rebuttals.response: That is a fair thought. Since no one can guarantee future rates, I would look at what this solves today and whether the savings or structure gives you enough benefit now.
rebuttals.followUp: If rates improved later and you still had flexibility, would solving the current payment issue now still be worth comparing?

rebuttals.label: Closing costs are high
rebuttals.response: I agree costs matter. The way I would judge it is by the break-even and whether the monthly or long-term benefit outweighs the cost over the time you expect to keep the loan.
rebuttals.followUp: Would it help if I showed a lender-credit version with less out-of-pocket cost?

rebuttals.label: Need to ask spouse
rebuttals.response: Absolutely. This is a household decision. Let me help you make that conversation simple by summarizing the goal, the payment impact, the costs, and the next step.
rebuttals.followUp: What is the biggest question they will probably ask first?

rebuttals.label: Do not reset term
rebuttals.response: That makes sense. Resetting the term is not the only way to structure this. We can compare a shorter term or payment-focused option and look at total interest.
rebuttals.followUp: Would you rather optimize for lowest payment or lowest total interest?

rebuttals.label: Shopping other lenders
rebuttals.response: Smart move—you should compare. Just make sure you compare locked Loan Estimates on the same day with the same points vs. lender credit so you do not get burned by hidden fees.
rebuttals.followUp: Have they given you an official locked Loan Estimate yet, or just a verbal quote?

title: Pivot Options
subtitle: Find another path to yes.
goal: Offer an alternate structure when the first option does not fit.
script: If the first structure is close but not quite right, pivot the loan design instead of ending the conversation.

options.title: Lender Credit
options.description: Trade a slightly higher rate for lower upfront cost when cash to close is the blocker.
options.talkTrack: If keeping costs down is the priority, we can bump the rate slightly and use a lender credit to cover most or all of the closing costs—shortening your break-even right away.

options.title: Shorter Term
options.description: Compare a 20-year or 15-year term when the borrower is worried about resetting the clock.
options.talkTrack: Instead of resetting back to 30 years, let's look at a 20- or 15-year custom term so you shave years off your mortgage and save tens of thousands in interest.

options.title: Payment Focus
options.description: Optimize for monthly relief when cash flow is the primary goal.
options.talkTrack: Let's stretch the term to maximize monthly cash-flow relief right now—you can always prepay principal whenever you want with zero penalty.

options.title: Follow-Up Plan
options.description: Set a specific date and reason to reconnect if the borrower is not ready today.
options.talkTrack: Let's lock in a 10-minute follow-up call for tomorrow after you've reviewed the numbers together, and I will set a rate-watch alert on your file in the meantime.
